literal: Virtue having considered, will bear I wonder the earth, back having looked mean words he who speaks' burden.
translation: I wonder if it is only out of a sense of duty to virtue that the earth bears the burden of a man who waits behind someone's back to speak mean words.
modern: ஒருவர் இல்லாத நேரம் பார்த்து அவரைப் பற்றி இழிவான சொற்களைப் பேசுபவனுடைய உடல் பாரத்தை, இதுவும் ஒரு தர்மம் என்று கருதித்தான் இந்தப் பூமி சுமக்கிறதோ?
explanation: This couplet marvels at the earth's patience in supporting the weight of a backbiter. The earth is traditionally praised for bearing all burdens, but the poet wonders if it only tolerates the backbiter out of a strict adherence to its duty (அறன்). The phrase 'புறன் நோக்கி' (looking at the back) vividly captures the cowardice of waiting for someone's absence to speak ill of them. By calling the backbiter a 'பொறை' (burden), the couplet emphasizes that such a person is nothing but dead weight on the world.
